## 🎞 An article as a story

A gallery in **Story** display mode becomes one **continuous scroll**: the article's images in document order, and **each image gets the panel its own shape deserves** — a wide panorama fills the card edge to edge, a tall portrait or a small file is centred at its native size (no letterboxing, no upscaling), a landscape work is split with the text beside it, and the text side alternates down the story. The article's own **top-level sections become chapters**, every panel is numbered, and a progress bar runs with the scroll.

The technique is ported from the [Met / Google-Arts-&-Culture prototype](https://github.com/fuzheado/met-gac-prototype) — one Wikipedia article in, an immersive gallery out — as a **display mode** rather than a new widget. Set **Display → Story** on any gallery and point it at an article. Drag the card taller for a longer view, and press **⛶ Present** (or add `?kiosk=1`) to give the story the whole screen.
